A Chinese court has frozen up to $300m of Nexperia-owned assets in China.

The court case is new. The supply-chain split isn’t.

Wingtech says Dongguan handles ~70% of Nexperia’s annual shipments. Its China unit has rebuilt local MOSFET and logic-IC supply, but transistors—54% of Q1 chip revenue—are still being shipped from existing inventory because overseas wafer supply remains cut off.

This gives Wingtech leverage. It doesn’t put the two sides back together.

Exactly. This is why AI capacity planning has to model the whole system, not just GPU and HBM shipments. TSMC’s Advanced Backend Fab 6 is designed for over 1 million 12-inch wafer-equivalents and more than 10 million testing hours per year—proof that packaging and testing are first-class capacity constraints.
@shao__meng 把“模型能力”和“Harness 加成”拆开了。报告里不同代码、视觉和自动化 benchmark 仍分别使用 DeepSeek Harness、Claude Code 或官方 scaffold；所以选 Coding Agent，不能只看模型榜单，得在自己的工具链和任务上测端到端完成率。

@nateberkopec That criticism is too broad. METR’s latest evaluations found frontier agents completing tasks that would take humans more than two full-time days, while its controlled trial found early-2025 AI systems still weren’t accelerating experienced developers. The useful safety work is
@shao__meng CS336 的含金量在于它不是“看懂 Transformer”就结束：官方作业一路做到 Triton FlashAttention、分布式训练、Common Crawl 清洗去重，以及用 RL 训练推理模型。想把 AI 变成生产力，建议把它当成一条完整模型生产链来练；CS221 再补上搜索、概率、决策和逻辑，知识才不容易被下一代模型架构带走。
@shao__meng 这其实把 Agent 的成本瓶颈说得很清楚：以后拼的不只是模型每秒吐多少 token，而是能复用多少上下文。前缀缓存的收益高度依赖命中率；命中率低，KV 被驱逐后就得重新计算，100 轮循环从 55 倍降到 10 倍不会自动发生。

@onusoz DeepSeek reports 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, but that result uses its own Minimal Harness with a 1M-token context. Independent work has already shown the same V4 Flash moving from 82.7% to 88.1% with harness adaptation, so your contamination concern is especially relevant: the
@_lopopolo Claude Code users approved roughly 93% of permission prompts, so permission boundaries matter. Human review can easily turn into rubber-stamping.
@onusoz If contamination is plausible, leaderboard wins mean a lot less. I’d test the same real agent tasks on a private, time-split eval first.
@jukan05 I'd wait before calling this a reshuffle. That's a 2Q26 ranking, while TrendForce still had Qualcomm third and AMD fourth for 2025.
@jukan05 The four-week-to-one-week claim is a real productivity signal, but I’d still want to know if verification and sign-off are included.
@shao__meng @thoma_gu 不错的学习资料，自己动手的话，Agent 先在内部试错再动手，才更接近可靠自动化，光给 LLM 再喂一批文本，生产力价值没那么大。
@shao__meng @gauri__gupta 这类笔记拿来搭知识地图挺好，真要降成本还是得按 workload 选优化，没实际经验建议不要直接硬背，面试会翻车
@jukan05 2028 is the number I'd watch. Packaging reliability, not chip design, may decide when AI hardware capacity actually shows up.
@shao__meng @LottieFiles 好工具，感谢分享！先把节奏、缓动和情绪判断对，再决定用 CSS、Framer Motion 还是 Lottie。
@shao__meng 我让codex学完这些课程，并提炼核心要素在自己的Agent Harness中，Agent 分数不能只看一个维度：METR看任务时长，GDPval首版偏一次性交付，DeepScholar-Bench偏研究综合和引用质量，生产里还得单独算验收和返工成本。

@quxiaoyin The U.S. still has the best model, but Stanford puts the lead at just 2.7% as of March. For real work, productivity, cost, access, and workflow fit matter more than a slim leaderboard lead.
@jukan05 Terafab still won’t add much compute anytime soon. A new fab takes 2–3 years to build, then another 1–2 years to ramp.
@quxiaoyin IPO pressure makes this tricky. I’d watch shipped task reliability and inference cost, not release cadence.
@WevolverApp Talking to the arm is a nice demo. I’d care more about whether it can detect a bad grasp and retry safely on its own.
@jukan05 50,000 wafers a month by 2027 sounds good, but with over half of Phase 3 equipment sourced in China, yield is what I’d watch for AI memory supply.
@Voxyz_ai I’d judge coding agents on whether they preserve the shared component system, not whether one page compiles.
@SemiAnalysis_ The gap is closing on some stacks, but this isn’t the default comparison: InferenceX puts GB300 at $0.06/M tokens versus $0.46 for MI355X on GLM5.1 at 30 tok/s/user.
@hxiao I’d treat the eval environment as part of the benchmark. Cursor found 63% of successful Opus 4.8 Max fixes were retrieved, not derived.
@MaxForAI Jev 如果真能在 70–500ms 内做结构化决策，还能给出校准后的置信度，我会先把它当自动化系统里的判断模块，接下来就看真实任务会错多少。
@gakonst I’d want to see Solar hold on real contracts: same gas, same bytecode size, fewer unsafe escape hatches. If it does, safer Solidity could mean less audit and maintenance work.
@jenzhuscott Pre-built AI workers are useful when they can run a workflow end to end, with permissions, retries, and human handoff. Otherwise, it's just a chatbot with a job title.
@laogui Radius 说白了就是先充 credits，再按模型用量结算，费用在上游价上加支付处理费，卖点是多模型路由和统一账单。

@SemiAnalysis_ The June 2 executive order points to early government access to powerful models without slowing deployment, so builders should watch access and compliance costs more than the label "regulation."
@MaxForAI 如果这轮谈成，Manus 公开披露的 ARR 已过 1 亿美元，至少说明 Agent 开始靠持续交付任务收费，不只是靠 demo 定价。不过说实话，Manus只适合新手用，产出质量真不如codex和claude
@damnang2 Agent 成本最后看权重和 KV cache 要搬几次，GPU 峰值算力再高也不顶用。
@shao__meng @JinaAI_ 91.14 这个分数不低，本地跑长文档解析，已经可以认真算成本了。
@tanayj Snap feels like the safest bet. AI Clips already turns one photo into a 5-second video, with distribution and monetization built in.
